text:
alex: heads-up: noticed a 12% p95 latency bump on qwen-70b when we enabled KV sharding + dynamic precision switching this morning
karina: ugh, saw traces too. regression started right after the kv_shard routing change?
yang: can you paste the sampleprof output? expecting conversion overhead from bf16->fp16 maybe
alex: pasted below (from the pod that hit it):
```
# sampleprof summary
kv_lookup: 34% cpu wait (memcpy+cast)
decode: 22% gpu
kernels: kernel_selector dispatch 3% overhead
batcher: 8% idle while cache conversion
```
karina: that 34% cpu wait is the tell. looks like we're doing eager cast+copy on cache miss/hit paths
sam: infra-bot rolled out the new shard router at 06:12 UTC :deploy: (canary 10% -> 100%)
alex: rollback isn't ideal; we need a short mitigation. hypothesis: when cache lives in bf16 on host and we cast to fp16 per-request, we pay copy+cpu cost and stall async cuda memcpy
yang: couple options: 1) keep quantized fp8/bf16 on-GPU pinned pages (memory cost), 2) lazy-cast only cache entries used in current batch, 3) move cast into kernel (fp16 kernels accept bf16 inputs and convert on-GPU)
karina: option 3 needs kernel change + verification for RoPE scaling correctness for qwen heads/kv dims. risky for canary.
sam: short-term we can change batcher to favor requests that reuse the same shard (batchshape tiling) to amortize cast cost. we already have a batch_shaper knob.
alex: ran quick experiment: pinned 8 pods to canary with batch_shaper=tiling, results: p95 dropped 7%, but throughput dropped 4% due to less optimal packing
yang: can you share the perf trace for one request so I can see device memcpy timings?
alex: attach snippet:
```
[trace]
HOST memcpy start +0.12ms
cast bf16->fp16 +0.9ms (cpu)
cudaMemcpyAsync start +1.1ms
kernel start +2.2ms
```
This is for prefetched prefix hit path
karina: confirms: cast on CPU is the bottleneck, especially for long prefix cache hits where many KV rows are touched
sam: is this specific to qwen layout (large kv_dim) vs llama?
yang: yes, qwen has wider kv dims and more contiguous rows -> bigger mem copies, so conversion cost scales badly
alex: proposed next steps: 1) revert shard router to previous routing within 2 hours if no quick mitigations, 2) enable batch_shaper=tiling in canary only, 3) prototype on-gpu cast kernel for bf16->fp16 and benchmark, 4) explore storing cache already quantized to fp16 on-GPU for hot prefixes
karina: assign: yang -> kernel prototype, alex -> canary tiling change + traces, sam -> rollback plan and deploy gating, i'll own correctness signoff for RoPE interactions
wang: (reaction) :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy status: canary tiling change applied to canary group (8 pods). monitoring p95 and cache-hit ratio.
yang: also flagging memory impact: pushing cache to GPU will increase device memory pressure; need eviction policy adjustment (lru -> size-aware)
alex: noted. i'll add ephemeral eviction thresholds for canary and watch OOMs
karina: nice triage. let's sync in 30m. if p95 not improving we'll rollback shard router. :eyes:
